newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar down sharply after CFTC data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar down sharply after CFTC data.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices slumped in early going Tuesday, led by sharp losses on the spot contract, as dealers sold heavily in response to Commitment of Traders data released last night, trading sources said.
The latest CFTC figures, which showed speculators to be net long nearly 24,000 lots (non-commercial plus non-reportable) as of December 31, sparked a rapid sell-off this morning.

"It attracted a lot of selling right from the open by the trade and producers," said one broker. He estimated that speculators had padded their long position by an additional 10,000 lots since the data was tallied.

March futures gapped 0.08 cent lower at the open, and commission houses joined the fray once nearby March dipped below 10.90 cents. A leading U.S. trade house aggressively sold the nearby switch, dragging March at one point to 0.10 cent under second-position May.
At 1137 EST, March futures were down 0.19 cent a lb, to 10.88 cents, having traded from 10.84 to 10.99. May was 0.13 lower, at 10.97, while the outer months were 0.04 to 0.12 lower.
An estimated 8,809 lots had been exchanged as of 1100 EST.
Chartists said the market found fairly solid support toward 10.80 cents. But the upside appeared limited, noting March's inability on Monday to clear resistance at 11.12 cents.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
